Rule 11 source row, re-read. Claude Code: output reaches the agent; SessionStart re-fires with source resume, compact and clear, and never at a subagent start. Codex: fires at startup, resume and clear; no SessionStart seen after /compact; output reaching the agent is **unproven**; trust is keyed per entry, and a new hook needs a new trust entry. Both: the plugin's SessionStart handlers timed out at 15 s in pane sessions. At SessionStart a plugin-enabled session runs 3 plugin commands, each through hooks/run-hook.py with --soft: install-git-hooks.sh --quiet (timeout 15 s), update-notice.sh (timeout 15 s) and repo-list SessionStart (timeout 60 s). hooks/hooks.codex.json holds the same 3 with ${PLUGIN_ROOT}.
The refused SDD draft row (its line 1123) says hooks/hooks.json:19 registers one SessionStart command; hooks/hooks.json registers 3 (:9, :14, :19), so its Existing-contract cell is wrong.

install-git-hooks.sh --quiet writes the reference-transaction stub (branch-name-gate.sh) and the pre-commit stub (precommit-gates.sh) into the common git hooks directory, only where the repository root has an .afk/ directory. It prints nothing on success and writes to stderr only when a non-AFK hook already exists.

update-notice.sh prints a notice ('AFK Toolkit X is out (you have Y).', any Migration lines and the newer changelog sections) only when the origin carries a higher SemVer tag; every failure path exits 0 in silence.

repo-list SessionStart runs the SessionStart handlers that the repository declares in .afk/hooks.json (or the file its repo-hooks key names). This repository declares none (.afk/hooks.json is [] and .afk/config.yaml has no repo-hooks key), so it returns 0 with no output. A SessionStart fault goes to stderr only, because SessionStart is not a blocking event.

Provider mapping: Claude Code reads hooks/hooks.json from the installed plugin at the default path (.claude-plugin/plugin.json has no hooks key; providers/CONFORMANCE.md:320 quotes the debug line that names the cached hooks\hooks.json). Codex reads hooks/hooks.codex.json through .codex-plugin/plugin.json:53, and its trust keys name that file (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:320). The adapters detect Claude Code by CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT or CLAUDECODE and Codex by PLUGIN_ROOT.

What depends on the chain: the git stubs that install-git-hooks.sh writes run hooks/branch-name-gate.sh on ref updates and hooks/precommit-gates.sh at agent commits, which runs the build-gate adapters through hooks/lib/adapter.sh. /afk:setup H5 and a manual run are the other install paths.

hooks/run-hook.py runs a plugin handler without capturing its output (:319), and afk_emit_context writes only a PreToolUse envelope (hooks/lib/provider.sh:116-124). No file under hooks/lib names SessionStart in any searched form (seed searches q-968e7350, q-b00fd552, q-3afe2a1f), so no helper emits SessionStart context: a short-form handler prints plain stdout.

SessionStart fires in pane agents on both harnesses: Claude Code at startup and again with source resume, compact and clear; Codex at startup, resume and clear, and not after /compact. On Claude Code no SessionStart fires at a subagent start (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:320).

On Claude Code SessionStart output reaches the agent: the probe agent quoted both nonces from its start context. Outputs arrive in finish order, not configuration order, and a 23.9 KB output arrived as 'Output too large (23.9KB)' with a saved file and a preview of lines 001-032, its last line not in context (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:320).

unverified: no repository document proves that Codex delivers SessionStart output to the agent. providers/CONFORMANCE.md:320 marks it **unproven** and its probe agent received no hook text at session start; the agent-written GRILL-LOG.md:489 says it reaches Codex, from trial log T12, which is not in the repository.
unverified: the repository does not state Codex's SessionStart output size limit or output order; providers/CONFORMANCE.md:320 states both for Claude Code only.

On Codex the plugin's hooks run only with features.hooks = true and a current trust entry per handler. The trust key is afk@afk-toolkit:hooks/hooks.codex.json:session_start:<group>:<index> and its value is a hash of the definition, so a release that changes hooks/hooks.codex.json asks the human to trust again.

The planned change does not reach every plugin-enabled Codex session: its new hooks.codex.json entry runs only after the human enables features.hooks and trusts that entry; Codex fires no SessionStart after /compact, so nothing prints the short form again after a Codex compaction; and even a trusted entry's output reaching the agent is unproven (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:320). The cell 'Every plugin-enabled session, on both harnesses' holds on Claude Code only, and there at session starts, not at subagent starts.

Append the short-form entry after the 3 existing SessionStart entries in both files: Codex keys trust by group and index, so an entry inserted before them gives the existing handlers new keys, which then need trust again before they run (inferred from the key shape).

In the pane-agent probes the plugin's own SessionStart handlers logged 'timed out after 15000ms' on Claude Code, and Codex showed 'Hook failed, hook timed out after 15s' at startup, after resume and after /clear (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:320). 15 s is the timeout of the install-git-hooks.sh and update-notice.sh entries (hooks/hooks.json:10, :15).

A short-form handler on the same path (python launcher, then a Git Bash spawn, a 15 s timeout) is exposed to the same timeouts in loaded pane sessions: the spawn cost degrades under load (hooks/README.md:31), and the plugin's SessionStart handlers already timed out there (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:320). A print-only handler was not probed.
unverified: whether a SessionStart handler that times out still delivers its output to the agent; no repository document states it for either harness.

The automatic gates check hooks/hooks.json only: rules E and J of hooks/native-contract-gate.sh read that file (:224-226, :262-283). The twin comparison with hooks/hooks.codex.json is only in hooks/tests/hook-smoke.sh:227-243, which no hook, gate script or CI workflow runs (T5: every line that names hook-smoke is a document or the script itself; T7: the only tests/ paths in CI, the hook scripts and both hook files are rule G's fixture check), and which exits 0 with SKIP when jq is missing. providers/PARITY.md:103, which says the native-contract gate diffs the twin, is refuted.
So an edit that adds the short-form entry to hooks/hooks.json only passes every automatic gate and leaves Codex without the handler.

Rule J accepts a hooks.json command only in the form python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/run-hook.py" [--soft] plugin <handler>.sh [args] or repo-list <event>; rule E accepts SessionStart (CAPABILITIES.md:26); rule I requires LF-only shell handlers.

Check A of hooks/native-contract-gate.sh scans every plugin *.md except PROVIDERS.md, CAPABILITIES.md and providers/CONFORMANCE.md for harness names (Claude Code, Codex), CLAUDECODE, PLUGIN_ROOT, SendMessage and subagent_type. The full rule in DELEGATION.md must state both branches without that vocabulary or carry an allow entry, or the gate goes red; a short form held in a hooks/*.sh handler is not scanned.

A short form declared in a repository's .afk/hooks.json (repo-list, the entry the draft cell names as the existing contract) runs only in repositories that declare it. To reach every plugin-enabled session the handler ships as hooks/<name>.sh behind its own plugin entry.

The opt-in boundary holds for a plugin-shipped SessionStart entry: hooks activate only through the harness that enables the plugin, and a disabled plugin leaves zero plugin hooks, so AC-041 (a session without the plugin is unchanged) holds.

Given the premise that the short form states both branches of the pane rule as fixed text and points at DELEGATION.md, the 2 branches are written twice, in the hook and in DELEGATION.md. That conflicts with AC-047 'stated once' and the one-home rule unless the hook reads its text from DELEGATION.md or a gate pins the copy; neither exists, and DELEGATION.md holds no pane-agent rule yet.

Same-commit duties for the new hook: FRESHNESS.md:64 (the command shape that rule J fixes, and a hook-smoke.sh case that would catch the defect) and FRESHNESS.md:40 (a CHANGELOG line under Unreleased); FRESHNESS.md:65 adds the conformance row when a live probe changes. The hooks lists in CLAUDE.md:201 and AGENTS.md:201 already name no SessionStart handler and say the plugin ships no PreToolUse handler, while hooks/hooks.json:31 and :36 register 2.
skills/afk/setup/MANIFEST.md:510-511 (O2, features.hooks) names only Stop gates and PreToolUse guards as needing the feature; the SessionStart handlers need it too (CAPABILITIES.md:8).
CAPABILITIES.md:33 spells the hook command as plugin|repo with no --soft; hooks/hooks.json uses '--soft plugin' and 'repo-list' (:9, :19).

No test runs install-git-hooks.sh or update-notice.sh: in T2 no line under a test directory names either script, and in T6 no test runs the commands of hooks/hooks.json (its hits are the twin comparison and .afk/hooks.json fixtures), while providers/PARITY.md:115 and :128 mark both covered by an automated gate.

The 3 existing SessionStart commands keep their contract when the short-form entry is appended after them: each runs as its own command with its own timeout in its own launcher process (hooks/hooks.json:9-20, hooks/run-hook.py:319), and on Codex their trust keys stay the same (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:271).

claims.text: The SessionStart chain also reaches the native-contract gate: the pre-commit hook that install-git-hooks.sh installs (hooks/install-git-hooks.sh:103) runs hooks/precommit-gates.sh at an agent commit, and that script runs the native-contract gate when the plugin tree lies inside the repository being committed and the staged paths touch it (hooks/precommit-gates.sh:138-154; hooks/lib/provider.sh:158-173). So, in the plugin's own checkout with the plugin root resolving into it, an agent commit that stages a hooks/hooks.json entry outside rule J's form is refused (hooks/precommit-gates.sh:162-166); with the plugin loaded from a harness cache outside the repository, the gate does not run at commit.

A short-form entry whose handler file is missing or misnamed prints nothing and turns no gate or test red: hooks/run-hook.py returns 0 with no output when the named handler is not in hooks/ (:314-318), hooks/tests/hook-smoke.sh:260-265 asserts exactly that silence, and rule J checks only the shape of the command (hooks/native-contract-gate.sh:262-283).

providers/PARITY.md:102 is refuted as well: it marks hooks/hooks.json covered by 'claude plugin validate .' and the registry gate, but hooks/skill-registry-gate.sh never reads hooks.json (the registration search returned no line of it; its hooks/ checks are the environment register and the adapter registry, :138-149, :194), and no script or CI workflow runs 'claude plugin validate .' (grep -rln 'plugin validate' over the repository's *.sh, *.yml, *.yaml and *.py files: no match; .github/workflows/release-gate.yml:37 runs only hooks/release-gate.sh).

The seed's B11 pass could not see how this repository registers handlers: its pattern matches only @...Listener, @Scheduled and @...Handler annotations (q-258772b6). The SessionStart handlers are registered as JSON command entries (hooks/hooks.json:9, :14, :19 and their twins in hooks/hooks.codex.json, which Codex loads through .codex-plugin/plugin.json:53), and the git hooks that handler 1 installs are registered by file name (hooks/install-git-hooks.sh:102-103). This walk adds the 19 registration lines as B11 nodes.

The git hooks that handler 1 installs outlive the session that installed them: install-git-hooks.sh writes them into the clone's shared hooks directory with the absolute plugin root (hooks/install-git-hooks.sh:19-26, :89-96), and they run the plugin's gates whenever that gate file exists and an agent marker is set (hooks/precommit-gates.sh:21-26, :42; hooks/branch-name-gate.sh:28-36). So an agent session in that clone runs them even with the plugin disabled, if its harness sets the marker (skills/afk/setup/MANIFEST.md:685: one harness sets CLAUDECODE). The planned print-only entry leaves nothing behind, so AC-041 still holds for it.

On Windows each plugin handler launch runs git before it starts bash, unless AFK_BASH or GIT_BASH names a shell: find_bash calls 'git --exec-path' with a 20 s timeout (hooks/run-hook.py:85-101, :104-115), longer than the 15 s timeout of the install-git-hooks.sh and update-notice.sh entries (hooks/hooks.json:10, :15). A short-form handler launched the same way pays that cost too; skills/afk/setup/MANIFEST.md:665 names AFK_BASH as the shell the launcher uses ahead of its lookup.

Once Codex trusts the short-form entry, later edits of its handler script raise no new trust prompt: trust covers the handler definition, not the script it runs (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:30). So a short form kept as fixed text in the script can change, and drift from DELEGATION.md, without any prompt; only an edit of the entry in hooks/hooks.codex.json asks for trust again (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:275).

skills/afk/setup/MANIFEST.md O4 says it is needed by every handler in hooks/hooks.json (:529, :533), but Codex keys trust on the entries of hooks/hooks.codex.json (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:271). After a release adds the short-form entry, O3 reports the Codex cache stale until it is refreshed, since its probe hashes hooks/hooks.codex.json (:519-522), and O4 reports the new handler untrusted until the human trusts it.

The documented hook command form 'plugin|repo <handler.sh>' (CAPABILITIES.md:33, hooks/README.md:19, docs/afk/agent-team-topology/research/FACTS-claude.md:32) names a 'repo' mode that does not exist: hooks/run-hook.py accepts only 'plugin' and 'repo-list' (:295), and rule J accepts only those two (hooks/native-contract-gate.sh:265-266).

The pane-agent probes ran the installed plugin 1.9.0 from the harness caches, not this worktree (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:310). This worktree's manifests say 1.3.0 (.claude-plugin/plugin.json:3) while the repository's tags reach v1.9.0, so in a session that loads the plugin from this worktree update-notice.sh compares 1.3.0 with the origin's highest tag (hooks/update-notice.sh:45-82) and, if the origin carries the same tags, prints every changelog section newer than 1.3.0. Each handler's output arrives on its own: in the probes outputs arrived in finish order, a 23.9 KB one as a saved file with a 32-line preview, and the agent still quoted a small output that finished after it (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:320).

Beyond the gates, the git hooks that handler 1 installs are relied on by /afk:execute and /afk:settle-change, whose agent commits run the commit-time gates (skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:59; skills/utils/settle-change/SKILL.md:59); by scripts/create-worktree, which checks a new branch name against the branch-name gate's pattern before git does (scripts/create-worktree:112); and by this feature's signed design, which counts the pre-commit gate as a control (docs/afk/agent-team-topology/GRILL-LOG.md:255; docs/afk/agent-team-topology/SDD.md:231). An appended print-only entry changes none of them.
On a machine where the launcher finds no bash, no SessionStart handler prints, a short form included: hooks/run-hook.py writes one stderr line and, with --soft, exits 0 (:302-308).

Every line of this walk that names SessionStart in any spelling the seed searched is already a seed node; the registration-side walk (4 searches, 210 lines over the whole repository) found no name-form site the seed missed.

The boundary does not hold that way for every plugin-shipped SessionStart entry. Handler 1, install-git-hooks.sh, writes 2 git hooks into the shared hooks directory of a clone whose root has .afk/, each naming the absolute plugin root (hooks/install-git-hooks.sh:47-56, :89-98). It only writes or rewrites them, and branch-name-gate.sh documents removal by hand (:5, :22). Each git hook runs its gate while the gate file at that root exists, and the gate acts on an agent marker, not on plugin enablement (hooks/install-git-hooks.sh:94-96; hooks/precommit-gates.sh:41-42; hooks/branch-name-gate.sh:26-36). What depends on handler 1 of the chain (install-git-hooks.sh) is the pair of git hooks it writes into the clone's shared hooks directory, only where the repository root has .afk/ (hooks/install-git-hooks.sh:47-56, :102-103). The reference-transaction hook runs hooks/branch-name-gate.sh on ref updates. The pre-commit hook runs hooks/precommit-gates.sh, which returns at once without an agent marker (:42). At an agent commit it runs the build-gate adapters through hooks/lib/adapter.sh (:57, :122-131), and the native-contract gate when the plugin tree lies inside the repository being committed and staged paths touch the plugin tree, .agents or .codex (:138-160; hooks/lib/provider.sh:158-179). The sites that rely on those hooks, judged over the ledger's nodes for every line naming them (q-da62488f, q-ea58d87c): the Stop dispatcher, which leaves the heavy code gates to commit time (hooks/stop-gates.sh:19-21); /afk:execute and /afk:settle-change, whose agent commits run the commit-time gates (skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:59; skills/utils/settle-change/SKILL.md:59); scripts/create-worktree, which checks a new branch name against the gate's pattern before git runs the gate (scripts/create-worktree:112); /afk:setup H5, which probes the installed stub for its marker and is, with a manual run, the other install path (skills/afk/setup/MANIFEST.md:76-77; hooks/install-git-hooks.sh:12-13); and the feature's design, which counts the pre-commit gate as a control (docs/afk/agent-team-topology/GRILL-LOG.md:255, :777; docs/afk/agent-team-topology/SDD.md:231, :240, :770).
